verdict: Caution: lend selectively to bought-leaf and small estate borrowers with auction receipts and clean stock statements; avoid leveraged estate-only exposures until liquidity stress eases.
title: Dibrugarh Tea Plantations: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A tea garden turns green leaf into made tea and cash through the auction floor, not the retail shelf.** Leaf is plucked, withered, rolled, fermented, dried and sorted within hours; the output is bulk tea sold largely at auction, so the grower is a price-taker on a commodity whose value sits in the leaf-to-made-tea conversion and the timing of sale. **Cash is locked in the garden and the warehouse, not in the brand.** Cost is dominated by plucking labour and fuel for drying; capex is modest but lumpy (factory, irrigation, replanting), and the working-capital cycle runs from monthly wage outflows to auction receipts weeks later. **So when a proposal lands, check the split between own-estate leaf and bought leaf, and ask for the last six months of auction sale statements before anything else.**

## What has changed now
**The local signal is liquidity stress, not demand collapse.** The Tea Board is expanding its auction network precisely as the industry faces liquidity stress [2], and the official data pack flags Assam electricity demand up only 1.9% Apr-to-date against India's 9.5% [D] — a local stress signal. **The headline price is a mirage for credit purposes.** A rare variety fetched Rs 75,000/kg at auction from Dikom Tea Estate [1], but that is a specialty lot, not the bulk invoice price your borrower realises. **Rating reports show the strong survive on balance sheet, not price:** TSAIL held Rs 65.68 crore of liquid investments at March 31, 2026 [8], and KDHP draws comfort from Tata Consumer linkages with 18% of FY2026 tea sold to TCPL [9].

## Where the growth is
**Pursue bought-leaf factories and small estates with direct buyer linkages, not leveraged legacy gardens.** The GST tailwind is real — Assam collections up 36.9% Apr-to-date versus India's 6.1% [D] — and the expanded auction network [2] widens the selling channel for borrowers who can deliver consistent lots. **Favour borrowers with a branded or export buyer contract**, mirroring the KDHP-TCPL model [9], and those with liquid reserves like TSAIL [8]. **Avoid estate-only borrowers with no auction receipts, no buyer contract and thin liquidity** — the liquidity stress [2] hits them first.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the auction cycle, not the harvest hope.** Sanction working capital sized to actual sale statements, with stock and receivables as primary security and a charge on the garden where title allows. **Take every month: auction sale statements, stock statements, wage-payment proof and a receivables ageing.** Set a covenant that drawing power is recalculated monthly from realised auction receipts, and require any buyer contract to be assigned. **If the borrower cannot produce auction statements, ask for the buyer's purchase confirmations and bank statements instead; if neither exists, decline.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the cash conversion, not the crop.** Falling auction realisations against the same grade, rising bought-leaf dependence, delayed wage payments, and stock ageing beyond the season are the first cracks. **If electricity demand in Assam stays below India's growth [D], read it as factory idle time and ask why.** If a borrower's sale statements show declining volumes while peers like Tyroon report profit swings on de-growing sales [6], pull the limit and re-assess.
watch: realisation falls below the borrower's cost line for two consecutive months -> cut drawing power and seek buyer contract
any delay beyond the statutory date -> freeze fresh disbursement and inspect cash flow
stock ageing crosses one season -> require liquidation plan and revalue security
stays below India's growth [D] for two more prints -> treat factory as under-utilised and re-price risk
contract lapses or buyer share falls -> downgrade internal grade and seek alternate offtake proof
